Convert a datetime format string into a regular expression

Source: R/utils.R
format_to_regex.Rd

Internal helper for birdnet_add_datetime(). Translates a strptime()-style format (e.g. "%Y%m%d_%H%M") into a regular expression that matches text of the same shape, so users can describe a file name pattern with a familiar format instead of writing a regex.

Usage

format_to_regex(fmt)

Arguments

fmt

A single character string giving a strptime()-style format.

Value

A single character string containing a regular expression (using lookarounds, so it needs the ICU engine used by stringr).

Details

Supported codes are %Y (4-digit year, 1900-2099), %y, %m, %d, %H, %M and %S (2 digits each). All other characters are matched literally, with regex special characters escaped. The regex only checks the shape of the text (the number of digits in each position), not whether the values are valid dates. That check is left to strptime(). The match is wrapped in lookarounds so it only matches a digit run of exactly this shape and never part of a longer run of digits (e.g. the prefix in 00014530_20230518T133500).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
format_to_regex("%Y%m%d_%H%M")

stringr::str_extract(
  "00014530_20230518T133500.WAV",
  format_to_regex("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")
)
} # }
